topics.topic: ProjectValidationResult lifecycle-field consistency and authoritative admission rule
questions: For creation of a viewer grant, staff assignment, or producer grant, is admission determined by `exists` plus `is_active`, by `status`, or must ProjectValidationResult guarantee that these fields can never disagree?
What consistency constraints bind `exists`, `is_active`, `status`, and `failure`, and which field is authoritative if they disagree?
Which combinations of `exists`, `status`, and `is_active` are valid, is `is_active` derived from `exists` and `status`, and which rule controls when the fields disagree?

quotes:
The project guard of A4 reads the validation answer's `exists`
(false → not found) and, for a mutation, its `status` (anything other than
`active` → `archived_project`); the grant and assignment creation
operations of access management (revocation consults no Registry, R0-24)
read `exists` and `is_active` instead (A6, State 1 M17)
and proceed only when both are true: `exists` false is refused as an
unknown project, otherwise `is_active` false as an archived one, each with
its own operation's error

A decoded validation answer is returned as it is and read by
its caller as A5 says; the two readings of A5 agree, because the Registry
sets `is_active = true` exactly when `status` is `active` (Registry v1
`validate_project_reference`). The portal does not check the fields of an
answer against each other: each caller acts on the field A5 names for it,
whatever the others say
judgement.why: State 2 specifies which fields each caller reads, states the Registry consistency guarantee, and explicitly says the portal does not resolve inconsistent answers itself.

topics.topic: Whether registry validation applies to revocation and operations beyond creation
questions: Does M17’s new requirement apply only to creation, or also to revocation and any other operation on a grant or assignment?
Does the new `exists && is_active` condition apply only when creating a viewer grant, staff assignment, or producer grant, or also when revoking one?

quotes:
Portal mutation policy admits the grant and assignment operations of
access management only on an answer whose `exists` and `is_active` are
both true (State 2 A5) and uses only `status` (`active` or not) in the
project guard of State 2 A4/A5; archived context remains readable.

Revoking an existing viewer grant, staff assignment or producer grant does not consult the
Registry and succeeds for an archived project, also while the Registry is
unavailable, so archival never stands in for revocation
judgement.why: The unqualified State 1 requirement covers access-management grant and assignment operations, while State 0 expressly exempts revocation from Registry validation.

bases.rests_on:
Creating and revoking grants and assignments are access management: they check the
session, the active principal and the administrator's access-management
capability (R0-14); creating one also requires the Registry project known and
active, revoking one consults no Registry (R0-24).

unavailable, so archival never stands in for revocation

unavailable, so archival never stands in for revocation

witness.initial: An active viewer grant exists for a Registry project that is archived while the Registry is unavailable.
events: An administrator with the access-management capability requests revocation of the viewer grant.
outcomes: The revocation succeeds without consulting Registry, and the grant becomes revoked.
The revocation cannot obtain an answer whose `exists` and `is_active` are both true, so it fails and the grant remains active.
witness.observer: The administrator and the viewer whose project access remains or is revoked.
basis:
Creating, revoking and re-issuing client viewers, their access links and
project grants, staff accounts and assignments, service principals, their
credentials and producer grants all require the access-management capability,
which only administrators hold (R2).

An existing grant or assignment is not new access: it keeps giving read
access, also after the viewer receives a new access link or the staff
account is reinstated, because neither operation consults the Registry

Revoking an existing viewer grant, staff assignment or producer grant does not consult the
Registry and succeeds for an archived project, also while the Registry is
unavailable, so archival never stands in for revocation
